records.name: Philadelphia Python Users Group (PhillyPUG)
records.summary: Python programmers who meet to hear talks and work on projects together. The group paused during the pandemic and restarted in May 2026 with a meetup at the University of Pennsylvania.
records.what_you_do: Attend the talks and join the project hack nights, which the restarted group plans to hold monthly. A yearly intro to Python class ran in past years.

schedule.text: Talks and monthly project hack nights are planned after the May 2026 restart. The group's Meetup page is where dates appear.

locations.label: Jon M. Huntsman Hall (May 2026 restart meetup)

cost.text: Not stated in the source checked

first_step.how: Join the group on Meetup (meetup.com/phillypug) to hear about the next talk or hack night.
first_step.basis: Public talks are announced through Meetup, and the source gives no membership requirement.

records.notes: The group's own site (phillypug.org) refused connection, so this record rests on one Technical.ly article dated May 26, 2026. The article says the restart meetup was on Wednesday, May 28, but May 28, 2026 is a Thursday, so only the month is used. The Intro to Python class is recorded as yearly in the past, with no current date.

records.name: Philadelphia County ARES (PCARES)
records.summary: Volunteer ham radio operators who provide emergency communications for the Southeastern Pennsylvania Red Cross, run radio nets, and train for disaster response.
records.what_you_do: Check into the Sunday evening net, take part in drills and Red Cross station activations, and train for emergency response. The group's site says no amateur radio license is required to join.

schedule.text: Net on Sundays at 8 pm on the Phil-Mont repeater, 147.030 MHz. The net is also carried on EchoLink and ALLSTAR.

first_step.how: Listen to or check into the Sunday 8 pm net on 147.030 MHz, or join by EchoLink or ALLSTAR. The site lists no sign-up form.
first_step.basis: Anyone may join and the regular net is a clear entry point, but the site lists no membership steps.

records.notes: The group's own site has no dated post after March 2024 (a Red Cross station activation). The 2025 evidence is the University of Pennsylvania ham club's Oct 18, 2025 luncheon handout, which lists the PCARES representative as a speaker. The net schedule on the site is not dated, so confirm it before relying on it.

records.name: University of Pennsylvania Amateur Radio Club (UPARC)
records.summary: Penn's campus ham radio club, whose call sign W3KZ dates to 1909. Its activities include Field Day, portable operating from parks and summits, high altitude balloon launches, and emergency drills.
records.what_you_do: Operate at Field Day and portable events, help with balloon launches and satellite workshops, and join emergency communications drills with local groups.

schedule.text: No regular meeting time was found on the club site. A luncheon was held on Oct 18, 2025, at Levine Hall, with a Zoom option.

locations.label: Campus station (address from the club's Oct 2025 handout)

first_step.how: Fill out the club's interest form, linked from its site. Membership is limited to Penn alumni, faculty, staff and students.
first_step.basis: Only Penn affiliates can join, and the first step is an interest form, so outside operators cannot take part.

records.notes: Membership is limited to Penn alumni, faculty, staff and students, so open_to is set to members, not public. The Oct 2025 handout is a PDF on the club's own site and was read from page images. The handout also names a Holmesburg ARC trustee and a Philadelphia County ARES speaker.

records.name: Philadelphia Linux User Group (PLUG)
records.summary: The Philadelphia area Linux user group. Its site lists three meeting areas (Central, North and West), an IRC chat room and announcement mailing lists.
records.what_you_do: Join the mailing list or the IRC chat to hear about meetings and talk with other Linux users.

schedule.text: The site names three meeting areas but lists no days, times or upcoming dates.

first_step.how: Subscribe to the group's mailing list, linked from phillylinux.org, or join its IRC chat.
first_step.basis: Public mailing lists and IRC are the stated ways in, but no current meeting date is shown.

records.notes: Dormant on the evidence of its own site, whose latest dated item is from November 2015, when a meeting space ended. A Meetup listing for a Jitsi-based PLUG Central event exists but was not read, since Meetup is lead only. Confirm with the mailing list before showing it as active. The site names a person as contact, which is not recorded here.

records.name: Philly 2600
records.summary: A monthly public meetup for people interested in technology and computer security. Attendees can use a pseudonym, and bringing friends is welcome.
records.what_you_do: Come to the first Friday meeting in person to talk about technology and security with other attendees. Some people go on to a nearby bar or restaurant afterward.

schedule.text: First Friday of every month. People usually arrive around 6 pm and stay until about 8:30 pm.

first_step.how: Come to the meeting in person. The site lists no sign-up step.
first_step.basis: The site describes the meeting as open to any technology enthusiast in a public space, with no sign-up step.

records.notes: Probably active because the site describes a standing monthly schedule and shows no dated posts. The site points to a Mastodon account for updates and cancellations; the handle is not recorded here. Meetings at 30th Street Station were paused for construction when the site was read. The bar stop afterward may be for people 21 and older.

records.name: DC215 (DEF CON Philly)
records.summary: The Philadelphia DEF CON group for security and hacking fans. It runs show and tell nights, open houses, workshops and capture the flag games, mostly at local venues.
records.what_you_do: Go to a show and tell, an open house or a pick night, and join the group's Discord to hear what is next.

schedule.text: No regular weekday is stated. Listed events: a Wednesday show and tell, a Friday open house, and a third Friday open pick night at Wooden Shoe Books, described as monthly. The site gives no year for these dates.

first_step.how: Join the group's Discord (invite link at the top of its site), then go to an open event.
first_step.basis: Open events and a Discord invite are listed, but the site does not say beginners are welcome.

records.notes: Event dates on the site have weekdays and days of the month but no year, so status stays unknown until someone confirms the current dates. Public access is inferred from the open events and a welcoming statement, not stated outright. A sponsorship email is on the site and is not recorded.

records.name: PhillyMesh (Philly Mesh)
records.summary: Hobbyists who build and run Meshtastic and MeshCore radio nodes across Greater Philadelphia, and who share how-to guides with others. They also experiment with AREDN mesh networks.
records.what_you_do: Join the Discord to ask questions, follow the Getting Started guides to set up a node, and try mesh experiments with other members.

schedule.text: No meeting schedule is listed. Community chat runs in a Discord linked from the site.

cost.text: No membership fee is mentioned on the site.

first_step.how: Join the Philly Radio and Mesh Discord, linked from phillymesh.net, then start with the Getting Started guides.
first_step.basis: The site has beginner guides and a public Discord, but does not say beginners are welcome at meetings.

records.notes: The last sign of life comes from post dates in the site's page addresses (Sept 2, 2026), since the page shows no visible date. The Discord was not opened. Iffy Books and Free Library events mentioning PhillyMesh appeared in search results only and were not used as sources.

records.name: IHM Center for Literacy
records.summary: An adult literacy center that supports immigrants' inclusion in American society. It teaches English and basic computer use, and it takes volunteer tutors and new students through a phone line and online forms.
records.what_you_do: Students build English, reading and computer skills. Volunteers tutor adult learners. Both paths start with a form or a phone call.

schedule.text: The class schedule was not found on the pages checked. The registration pages are labeled for the 2025 to 2026 year.

cost.text: Not stated on the pages checked

first_step.how: Call 215-338-3120, or use the student interest form or the volunteer form linked from the site.
first_step.basis: A phone line and two interest forms are published, but eligibility, class levels and fees are not stated.

records.notes: Probably active: the site has registration and calendar pages for 2025 to 2026 and a 2025 copyright, which are not dated to a month. The site does not show a street address. A 2015 article places the center in West Philadelphia, and that is the only source for the location. Eligibility, class levels and cost are unknown; verify before publishing.

notes: Second sweep of making-tech. Searches: 10 of 10 used, the hard cap. Fetches: 33. Records: 9 (8 publish, 1 hide), all tier 1. Most search results were roundups dated 2019 to 2023, so many Meetup-only groups are leads, and Meetup pages were not read for facts. Gaps with no current source found: woodturning guilds open to the public, FIRST volunteer sign-up for Philadelphia teams, car and motorcycle clubs with public meets (the one cruise night seen, 215 Mopar Car Club's Philly Phridays at 9130 Academy Rd, appeared only in a search result and was not opened, so it needs a fetch next sweep), repair cafes (no search budget left), and current women and BIPOC in tech groups beyond the ones on the existing list. Skipped as already on the existing list: Philly Tech Sistas, Power Up Tech Corps, Code for Philly, DataPhilly, Hive76, NextFab, Philly Fixers Guild, Philadelphia Red Hat User Group, Philly AI Connect, Mid Atlantic Amateur Radio Club, Philadelphia Furniture Workshop. Skipped as out of area: Road Angels of Doylestown (Bucks County cruise night), Cruisin' Classics (Chester County), a South Jersey woodworkers guild (Cherry Hill, NJ), Suburban Philly Cloud and DevOps (Malvern), OWASP King of Prussia, and the Blue Bell AWS user group. Illegal street car meets in police coverage were not listed. Dormancy and staleness: PLUG is dormant on its own site's last dated item (Nov 2015); DC215 has no years on its event dates, so its status is unknown; PCARES is active on an Oct 2025 club handout, though its own site's newest dated post is March 2024. The Penn club handout (Oct 18, 2025) is a PDF on the club's own site and was read from page images. PhillyPUG's source article gives a weekday that does not match May 28, 2026, so only the month is used. Girl Develop It's national site names no Philadelphia chapter. ChickTech's national site says it has closed; the Philadelphia chapter is hidden as defunct on that notice. Lesbians Who Tech Philadelphia, Women in Tech Network, Philadelphia Women in GIS and FemmeHacks were seen only in search results and are not listed.
